data.content_ref: inline:The target claims a large service is more resilient because its global control plane enables faster traffic evacuation, but its own second countercondition (poison pill passed with traffic) shows the evacuation mechanism can become the correlated-failure vector: shifting traffic to healthy segments injects the failure into them too. The argument therefore only works for failures that are not content-borne or config-borne. It also ignores that a global control plane is itself a shared cause that can turn an isolated fault into a synchronized one (its first countercondition), exactly the correlated-failure class the problem is concerned with. So the covering principle it relies on — 'central coordination improves resilience' — fails precisely for the correlated-failure regime the problem targets.
